messages.subject: "invalid next size" errors in featurecounts
parts:
Dear Wei and list,

Our collaborators are running into a non-deterministic error running featurecounts on a large dataset of BAM files. 

Command run:
featureCounts -s 2 -f -B -C -p -F SAF -T 4 -a gc_human_38.saf -o exon_tight_counts.txt 130418_4.bam

This is the error message and I have copied the full output below.

*** Error in `/lrlhps/users/rx90842/tools/subread-1.4.6-p5-Linux-x86_64/bin/featureCounts': free(): invalid next size (normal): 0x00002b10dc023400 ***
*** Error in `/lrlhps/users/rx90842/tools/subread-1.4.6-p5-Linux-x86_64/bin/featureCounts': free(): invalid next size (normal): 0x00002b10dc0274a0 ***

We find that running exactly the same command on the same input file gives this error sometimes, but not always.

Can you suggest what might be the source of this problem? Please let me know what additional information I can provide to help diagnose.

messages.subject: Re: "invalid next size" errors in featurecounts
parts:
Thanks!

It seems that you built the package from the source codes, hence the addressed in your executable file differ from mine. It is hard to tell what went wrong from the screen outputs.

Can you please provide your BAM file and the annotation file so I can find the bug from my side?

messages.author: 03099a56c65a7c28
messages.subject: Re: "invalid next size" errors in featurecounts
parts: It looks like I had a bug in my script for generating the SAF file that caused the ends of some of the regions to appear before the beginnings of those regions.  No that I have fixed that script to make a valid SAF file, everything is working.  It would be great if you could add something that check for this and prints a meaningful error message so that future users who do this can easily figure out why featureCounts is not working.  Thanks for all of your help!

messages.author: bce99ba71cd48eea
messages.subject: Re: "invalid next size" errors in featurecounts
parts: Glad to know that the bug was fixed. However, featureCounts should be able to identify such semantic issues in the input files, then stop running after reporting an error message. Can you please post a few lines in your annotation file with the issue so I can see why featureCounts didn't found it?
